diseases.name: Grasserie (Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus - BmNPV)
diseases.cause: BmNPV (Bombyx mori Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus). Spreads rapidly during high temperature and high humidity periods.
diseases.treatment: No cure for infected worms. Immediately isolate and destroy affected larvae.
prevention: Dust mandatory bed disinfectant (e.g., Vijetha, Ankush, or Sanjeevini) at 3g/sq.ft after each moult
Maintain ideal rearing house temperature (24-26°C) and humidity (70-75%)
Provide maximum ventilation to reduce accumulation of viral particles
Disinfect rearing equipment with 2% formalin solution before starting batch
diseases.silkworm_impact: 100% fatal for infected worms. Uncontrolled outbreaks can wipe out 80-90% of total cocoon crop.

diseases.name: Flacherie (Bacterial / Infectious Flacherie)
diseases.cause: Bacterial infection (Streptococcus, Bacillus) or Iflavirus triggered by feeding poor quality, fermented, or wet leaves.
diseases.treatment: Remove infected larvae using chopsticks. Disinfect bed with lime powder + bed disinfectant.
prevention: Never feed wet, dusty, overgrown, or leaf-spot infected mulberry leaves
Avoid overcrowded rearing trays; maintain proper larval density per bed area
Dust lime powder (100g/sq.m) to keep bed dry during high humidity days
Maintain strict hygienic hand washing before handling feed or larvae
diseases.silkworm_impact: Severe reduction in cocoon quality; affected larvae die prior to spinning or spin thin melt cocoons.

diseases.name: Muscardine (White / Green Fungal Muscardine)
diseases.cause: Fungal pathogen Beauveria bassiana. Fungal spores germinate on larval skin during cold, humid weather.
diseases.treatment: Dust Dithane M-45 (1%) mixed with slaked lime powder immediately across all trays.
prevention: Dust Captan / Dithane M-45 + Lime mixture (1:99 ratio) on larvae after every moult
Keep rearing room temperature above 25°C and reduce humidity below 70%
Burn all mummified chalky white larval corpses immediately — do not leave in room
Ensure air circulation using exhaust fans to prevent spore accumulation
diseases.silkworm_impact: Larvae die rapidly and become hard chalky mummies, releasing millions of infectious spores into rearing hall.

diseases.name: Pebrine (Microsporidian Disease - Nosema bombycis)
diseases.cause: Microsporidian parasite Nosema bombycis transmitted vertically from moth to egg or horizontally via contaminated food.
diseases.treatment: No cure. Transmitted via mother moth. Whole batch must be safely destroyed under guidance.
prevention: Procure certified disease-free layings (DFLs) only from recognized grainages
Conduct mother moth microscopic examination before egg incubation
Disinfect grainages and rearing houses with 2% formalin + 0.5% bleaching powder
Destroy any batch displaying pepper-like dark spots on integument
diseases.silkworm_impact: Total crop loss across successive generations if transovarial transmission occurs.

symptoms.label: Larvae become sluggish and slow-moving
Larvae stop feeding completely
Body becomes swollen and shiny
Skin breaks easily with slight pressure
Milky white hemolymph / fluid leaks from body
Worms crawl restlessly toward tray rims / walls
Swelling between body segments
Head tilted upward or held unnaturally
Body becomes soft, limp, and flaccid
Vomiting brown or clear digestive fluid
Foul or decaying smell from rearing bed
Body turns dark brown or black after death
Soft, wet feces or sticky diarrhea
White powdery fungal growth covers dead worm
Dead corpse becomes hard and chalky white
Corpse is stiff like a piece of wood/chalk
Irregular reddish or pinkish specks on skin
Black or dark pepper-like tiny spots on skin
Uneven growth rates (some worms tiny, some big)
Worms fail to enter or settle for moult properly
